oneLiner: 物体在平衡位置附近往复运动，回复力与位移成正比、方向相反。
oneLinerEn: Oscillation about equilibrium with restoring force proportional to displacement.
detail: F=−kx，加速度 a=−(k/m)x；位移随时间按正弦变化。典型模型：弹簧振子、小摆角单摆。
detailEn: F=−kx so a=−(k/m)x; displacement varies sinusoidally. Models: spring oscillator, small-angle pendulum.

oneLiner: 完成一次全振动的时间叫周期 T，每秒振动次数叫频率 f，二者互为倒数。
oneLinerEn: Period T is time per cycle, frequency f is cycles per second; they are reciprocals.
detail: T=1/f；单摆周期 T=2π√(L/g) 只与摆长和重力加速度有关、与质量无关（小摆角）。
detailEn: T=1/f; a pendulum's T=2π√(L/g) depends on length and g only, not mass (small angles).

oneLiner: 振动在介质中传播形成波，波速等于波长乘以频率。
oneLinerEn: A wave is vibration traveling through a medium; speed equals wavelength times frequency.
detail: v=λf；波传播的是振动形式与能量，介质质点并不随波迁移。分横波（如弦波）与纵波（如声波）。
detailEn: v=λf; waves carry form and energy, not matter. Transverse (string) vs longitudinal (sound).

oneLiner: 两列相干波相遇时位移叠加，形成加强区与减弱区。
oneLinerEn: Overlapping coherent waves add, giving constructive and destructive regions.
detail: 频率相同、相位差恒定的相干波才能产生稳定干涉；路程差为波长整数倍加强、半整数倍减弱。衍射则是一切波共有的绕过障碍物现象。
detailEn: Stable interference needs equal frequency and constant phase; integer wavelengths reinforce, half-integers cancel. Diffraction lets waves bend around obstacles.

oneLiner: 两列同向反向波叠加形成驻定波形；驱动力频率接近固有频率时振幅最大即共振。
oneLinerEn: Counter-traveling waves form standing patterns; driving near natural frequency maximizes amplitude (resonance).
detail: 弦乐器、管乐器的音高源于驻波的波长；塔科马大桥风毁是共振破坏的经典案例。
detailEn: String and wind instrument pitches arise from standing waves; the Tacoma Narrows collapse shows destructive resonance.

oneLiner: y–x 图看某一时刻所有质点的位置，y–t 图看某一个质点随时间的位移。
oneLinerEn: A y–x graph shows every particle at one instant; a y–t graph shows one particle through time.
detail: 波动图象的横轴是位置，相邻两波峰之间直接读出波长；振动图象的横轴是时间，一次完整起伏的宽度即周期，两图合体再用 v=λ/T 求波速。判断传播方向常用“带动法”：先振动的质点带动后振动的质点，故波形沿传播方向平移少许即可比出各点下一时刻的动向。最典型的易错是把 y–x 快照误当成某质点的振动历史——两图形状一样、含义完全不同；反之由振动图推各质点位置时，须先确认所给时刻。
detailEn: On a y–x graph the horizontal axis is position, so adjacent crests give the wavelength directly; on a y–t graph it is time, so one full excursion gives the period, and together they yield v=λ/T. To find the direction of travel, shift the whole waveform a little along the guessed direction and compare: whichever way fits the observed particle motions is the true one. The classic error is reading a y–x snapshot as a particle's history—the two curves look identical but mean different things, and going from a y–t graph back to positions requires fixing the instant first.

oneLiner: 波面上每一点都可视为发出子波的新波源，各子波的包络就是下一时刻的波面。
oneLinerEn: Every point of a wavefront emits a secondary wavelet; the envelope of all of them is the next wavefront.
detail: 这一作图同时解释了波的反射、折射与衍射：波进入波速较小的介质时，同一波面上各点子波前进的距离变短，包线遂转向法线一侧——频率保持不变，波速与波长同比例减小。它也给出衍射明显的条件：障碍物或孔径的尺寸与波长可比时子波绕得很远，尺寸远大于波长时阴影边界锐利、近似直线传播。原原理只定出波面的几何位置，不回答各方向各分配多少能量，后由菲涅耳补上子波相干叠加，才成为可定量使用的惠更斯–菲涅耳原理。
detailEn: The construction explains reflection, refraction and diffraction at once: entering a slower medium shortens every secondary wavelet on the same front, tilting the envelope toward the normal while frequency holds and speed and wavelength shrink together. It also sets the condition for strong diffraction—an obstacle or aperture comparable to the wavelength is wrapped around substantially, whereas one far larger leaves a sharp shadow and near-rectilinear travel. The original principle fixes only wavefront geometry, not how much energy goes each way; Fresnel added coherent superposition of the wavelets, making it the quantitatively usable Huygens–Fresnel principle.

oneLiner: 两列频率相近的波叠加，强弱会周期性地起伏，起伏频率等于两频率之差。
oneLinerEn: Two waves of nearby frequencies add into a pulsation whose rate is their difference.
detail: f₁ 与 f₂ 相差不大时，两波时而同相加强、时而反相抵消，每秒强弱变化的次数即拍频 |f₁−f₂|。拍是叠加造成的效果而非新的波：介质中各点仍同时参与两个频率的振动。调音师靠听拍判断音准——拍频越大相差越远，拍消失即已同频；超声血流计与雷达测速则把拍频（差频）与多普勒频移配合使用来读出速度。注意与驻波区分：驻波由同频率、相向传播的两列波形成，节与腹的位置固定；拍则是各点振幅随时间的起伏。
detailEn: With f₁ and f₂ close, the pair alternately reinforces and cancels, and the number of swellings per second—the beat frequency—is |f₁−f₂|. A beat is an effect of superposition, not a third wave: each particle still takes part in both original oscillations. Tuners listen for beats to judge pitch, a fast beat meaning a wide gap and silence on them meaning unison; ultrasonic blood-flow meters and radar speed guns combine the difference frequency with the Doppler shift to read out speed. Standing waves are different: made from two equal-frequency counter-traveling waves, they hold nodes and antinodes fixed in space, whereas beats are an amplitude that pulses in time.
